title: Team Power Level Award
doc: CKF Hard Mode - Team Power Level award.
Team PL is a SUM over GameMissionScoreModel joined to MissionPowerLevelModel
on (ActionClass, MissionPowerLevel). 'table' below is the reference copy
of the game's values: the mod reconciles against it before it
substitutes anything, and editing it changes no award. 'override' is
what you edit.
It is a sum, not a counter, and that was verified exactly rather than
approximately: the reference save's 127 mission rows sum to 7.7075 and its
first 126 to 7.6925, which are the two numbers the trace printed either side
of the insert that finished a PL 7 solo hack (Progression.cs:12-20).
The row itself carries no number. GameMissionScoreModel has six columns and
no fraction among them - Id, MissionTypeId, MissionPowerLevel, ActionClass,
GameTurn, MissionSuccessful - so the award is entirely a function of the two
join keys (Progression.cs:26-32).
ACTIONCLASS - settled by the save, not inferred. Every one of the reference
save's 127 completed missions was classed by the game itself
(Progression.cs:70-81):
0  LEGWORK only, always PL 0, always worth nothing
1  story missions and Power Play missions
2  Treaty contracts - the standard proc-gen board
3  solo hacks - every HackCPU / HackFile / HackLoot, whatever generated it
Class 3 wins over its source: M_PGenPower_Icarus_M1_HackCPU is class 3, not
1, and M_PGenTreaty_HackCPU is class 3, not 2.
Class 0 is worth nothing because the game's table has no class-0 band, not
because the sum skips those rows: a row whose (ActionClass, MissionPowerLevel)
has no cell contributes zero, and the arithmetic reconciles only if the 34
LEGWORK rows at (0, 0) are worth zero (Progression.cs:22-24, 142-144).
The victory screen reads a different path at a different time. The label rules
that make it agree are generated into ckf.hardmode.d/ from 'override' - see the
mirror invariant. Do not hand-write MissionPowerLevelModel rules in any overlay.
uiDoc: Your Team Power Level is a running total over every mission the crew has finished. Each completed mission is worth a fraction, looked up by what class of mission it was and what level it was at, and the total is the sum of all of them. This page replaces that table.
The new PL gains apply to missions you have already finished, which means you may see your PL spike up or down when you first load in.
The reference table is a copy of the game's own values, for comparison.
The four mission classes are 0 for legwork, which grants nothing; 1 for story and Power Play missions; 2 for typical proc-gen missions; and 3 for solo hacks.

To tell it is working, look for the reconcile line in the log: before substituting anything the mod adds up the game's own values over the same missions and checks that its total matches. If that line is not there, it could not reproduce the game's total and has deliberately left your Team Power Level exactly as the game computed it.

fields.label: Enable Team Power Level Award
fields.doc: Slice toggle. It lives in ckf.hardmode.cfg because a gate cannot live inside the file it gates, and the .cfg is parsed before anything else loads. Slices.Init binds every [Slices] key above the [General] Enabled bail-out, so BepInEx writes the line even when the mod is off. A key that cannot be read is reported at Error and treated as on. Off: the subsystem logs why and does nothing this launch. The retired "enabled" key inside the subsystem's JSON file is still parsed (RetiredEnabled) so that Slices.ReportRetiredGate can report it: a Warning, or an Error when it is false and this key is not. Nothing branches on it. The key is named for the subsystem, Progression; its file is teampl.json. It also gates ckf.hardmode.d/MissionPowerLevelModel.generated.json (Slices.OverlayOwner), the victory-screen label mirror of the award. scripts/gen_teampl_labels.py writes it from teampl.override merged over teampl.table, and serve.py regenerates it in the same save. It reaches the game through the overlay path: a .json in ckf.hardmode.d is an ordinary rules file, so ModelRules postfixes the materialised MissionPowerLevelModel row the victory screen re-reads, while Progression postfixes GameDb.SumGameMissionScore, a SQL aggregate that materialises no row. Two layers, one number. The slice claims the mirror so that turning Progression off cannot leave a stock award with a modded label.
fields.uiDoc: Turn this off and this part of the mod does nothing; the game uses its own values. The master switch on the first page turns off everything at once.

fields.label: Game's own table (reference)
fields.uiDoc: The game's own values, for reference. The mod checks its own arithmetic against these before substituting.
fields.doc: Reference copy of the game's MissionPowerLevelModel values. The mod checks its own arithmetic against these before substituting. Editing changes no award and can make the reconcile fail, which silently disables the retroactive path. The game's table has 63 cells: classes 1-3 across MissionPowerLevel 0-10, plus a negative-level band from -1 to -10 whose fractions are negative [measured]. Regenerate it from sheets/raw/MissionPowerLevelModel.csv if the game updates. [unverified: no negative level has been seen on an awarded row, and their purpose is unknown.]

fields.label: Award override
fields.uiDoc: Per-cell replacement of PL gains. A cell absent here keeps its reference value. I've picked the initial numbers to roughly have completionist playthroughs end around PL 10 and keep PL gains flat in order to have enemies continue scaling at a similar pace in the late game.
fields.doc: Per-cell replacement for the award. A cell absent here keeps its 'table' value, and a cell present here replaces it outright - the value is used verbatim, with no snapping to a game cell and no clamp of any kind in the code (Progression.cs:150-152, 340-342). A cell with no 'table' value works too: it simply contributes its own figure to the sum, and gen_teampl_labels.py emits its label rule marked '(no stock cell)'. THE RANGES BELOW ARE GUARD RAILS FOR THE EDITOR, NOT ENGINE LIMITS. ActionClass runs 0-3 because that is what the save files rows under; the game's table has no class-0 band, so a class-0 override has no stock value behind it and re-prices every LEGWORK row from zero. PowerLevelFraction is allowed to go negative because the game's own table does. A worked example: an override cell of ActionClass 2, MissionPowerLevel 7, PowerLevelFraction 0.015 makes Treaty contracts at PL 7 pay a solo hack's rate, 0.03 down to 0.015, and setting the same cell to 0 stops that class and level advancing the team at all.

invariants.reason: The award is a SQL aggregate that materialises no row; the victory screen re-reads the materialiser. Two layers, one number. The drift was measured: a rule set to 3.0 printed 'Team gained 3 PL' while the sum moved 0.015. scripts/gen_teampl_labels.py is what writes the target: regenerate it after editing 'override' and never hand-edit it. It emits a rule only for cells whose merged value differs from the game's own, so an unchanged run reproduces the file byte for byte.

Progression alone gives a correct award with a stock label; ModelRules alone gives a stock award with a lying label. Neither direction logs anything. check_schema.py reports a half-on pair as INVARIANT, which the editor refuses to save. A run that cannot read both keys (for example under --no-cfg) does not compare the pair; it prints a SKIPPED line and counts it on the 'linkedEnable:' census line.
